description: Same defect as WIN-010.c17 hole 0 and hole 1, repeated on other surfaces. (1) Chapman (1933, doi 10.1029/TE038i003p00175) is presented as having identified, documented or confirmed eclipse magnetic effects. Its Crossref abstract says the opposite: Chapman inferred what an E-layer Sq system would do in an eclipse, then judged the eclipse observations then available showed no regular effect of that type, pending further observations. It is the first theoretical statement, not a detection. (2) A "5–25 nT" standard-physics range ("confirmed across dozens of eclipses") appears with no source; it is the untraced-number pattern Erratum 1 E-3 found in B1-M-001. The best Boulder-specific evidence (Meza et al. 2022, doi 10.1016/j.asr.2021.07.029; our BOU 2017 INTERMAGNET check) shows the eclipse effect there mainly in X (about +10 nT) with Z small and positive, so a one-signed Z range is itself a misstatement of standard physics; the sign of dZ depends on station position relative to the shadow. KS-005 "Any result in 5–30 nT confirms both models" inherits both problems. A defender opening Chapman 1933 gets an easy "your founding paper says the effect was not seen" line on every one of these surfaces.
